summary: Iter 33 image-upload feature tested end-to-end. Backend: 9/9 pytest GREEN (upload for staff/service/product kinds, roundtrip GET /api/files/{id} with exact bytes, size 413, invalid mime 400, empty 400, unauthenticated 401/403, tenant-scoped file_ids, missing file 404, Cache-Control immutable at origin). Frontend: Staff + Inventory ImageUploader flows GREEN (Choose from laptop → toast → preview → /api/files/<uuid> URL population → clear button → paste-URL backwards compat → client-side .pdf rejection). REGRESSION: TenantBrandMark and Daily Report banner both still working. CRITICAL BUG: Services page was NOT wired to ImageUploader — it still uses a plain text <input> for Image URL despite importing the component. The image-uploader-service testid does not render anywhere in the app.

minor.issue: Backend correctly returns 'Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable' (verified via localhost:8001), but the Kubernetes/Cloudflare ingress in front of the preview URL rewrites this to 'no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate'. Browsers hitting the public URL will not cache images. Non-blocking for functionality but the intended perf win is neutralized in the preview environment. Test asserts backend header directly to isolate.

ui_bugs.issue: ImageUploader is imported (line 5) but never rendered — the Image URL field in the New Service modal is still a plain <input type='text'> on line 106. This means salon admins cannot upload service thumbnails from their laptop. data-testid='image-uploader-service' does not exist anywhere in the DOM.

action_items: Replace the plain '<input>' for Image URL on Services.jsx line 106 with '<ImageUploader kind="service" value={form.image_url} onChange={(url) => setForm({ ...form, image_url: url })} />' — matches the exact pattern already used in Staff.jsx line 90 and Inventory.jsx line 120.

OPTIONAL: Investigate the ingress Cache-Control override — if the preview/prod ingress can be configured to pass through Cache-Control for /api/files/* the immutable-caching perf win will materialise. Not urgent — feature works, just extra bandwidth.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py _init_storage/_put_object/_get_object correctly handle 403 (session expired) with a single retry after re-init — good defensive pattern.

server.py upload_image validates extension → size → emptiness in the right order; storage_path is tenant-scoped (miracurl-salon/tenants/<tenant_id>/<kind>/<uuid>.<ext>) — cross-tenant leak is impossible even if UUIDs collided.
GET /api/files/{id} intentionally has no auth — safe because the UUID is unguessable. This matches the Instagram-CDN pattern documented in the review request.
ImageUploader.jsx client-side validation mirrors server rules (mime + 3MB) — good UX, saves a round-trip on obvious rejections.
Services.jsx uses ImageUploader in import but not in JSX — likely a forgotten refactor. Staff.jsx and Inventory.jsx both wired correctly on lines 90 and 120 respectively.

server.py startup event catches init failures and logs a warning — verified: EMERGENT_LLM_KEY is present in .env so init succeeds. First upload without a key would raise HTTPException(500, 'Object storage not configured (EMERGENT_LLM_KEY missing)') — matches expected behavior in review request.

success_rate.frontend: 80% (Staff GREEN, Inventory GREEN, Services BROKEN — component not wired)

test_credentials: admin@miracurl.com / Miracurl@123 and owner@elegance.com / Owner@123 — both worked; EMERGENT_LLM_KEY present in backend/.env and storage init succeeded.
seed_data_creation: Test uploads created some 288-byte PNG entries in the uploads collection tagged with tenant_id (miracurl and elegance). No user-visible seed pollution. TEST_UploadStaff was NOT persisted (name field lookup failed in Playwright — irrelevant to the feature being tested; the upload itself succeeded).
